**The third**: that the humble is the most favored with people and the most beloved by them, and the most disposed to gather with them and to walk in their way. It has been said of one of the princes that, when he walked, he hurried in his pace; he was asked the reason for that, and he said: "Because it is more remote from vanity, and quicker for the meeting of need." One of the scholars was asked: "By what have you become a leader over the people of your time?" He said: "Because I have not met one of them but I have seen for him an excellence over me. If he was more knowledgeable than I, I said: 'This one is more obedient to God than I, on account of the surplus of his knowledge over mine.' If he was less knowledgeable than I, I said: 'This one's reckoning on the Day of the Resurrection is lighter than mine; for I disobeyed God deliberately, while he disobeys Him inadvertently.' If he was greater than I in age, I said: 'This one has more good deeds than I, on account of his preceding me in this world.' If he was less than I in age, I said: 'This one has fewer sins with God than I.' If he was equal to me in age and knowledge, I said: 'Perhaps his inner being is more sound for God than mine; for I know what has gone before me of sins, and I know nothing of what has been from him.' So I never cease honoring all of them and humbling myself before them." For this reason our early ones (peace be upon them) said: "Judge every person on the side of merit" (m. Avot 1:6); and they said: "Receive every person with a beautiful expression of face" (m. Avot 1:15); and they said: "Be lowly of spirit before everyone" (m. Avot 4:10); and they said: "A man should always be soft as a reed and not be hard as a cedar; on this account the reed merited that with it should be written the Torah-scroll, the *tefillin*, and the *mezuzot*" (b. Taʿanit 20a).

As for those that are in the matters of the next world —

**The fourth**: the humble is closer to the attainment of knowledge, by his submission to the scholars and his devotion to them and his aiming at them, as He said: "He who walks with the wise becomes wise" (Proverbs 13:20); and our early ones (of blessed memory) said: "Let your house be a meeting-place for the wise; sit in the dust of their feet, and drink in their words with thirst" (m. Avot 1:4). The aid from God upon knowledge is made valid for him by it, as He said: "He shall guide the humble in justice and shall teach the humble His way" (Psalms 25:9). The proud man — for him no true reality of knowledge is firmly fixed and he reaches no end-point of certainty of acquaintance, on account of his elevation away from aiming at the people of knowledge of God and of His Law — as He said: "The wicked, in his lofty nose, does not seek; God is not in any of his thoughts" (Psalms 10:4).

**The fifth**: that the humble hastens to the working of obediences with diligence, alertness, and eagerness; he is not haughty against any of that, nor does he despise anything of it — as our early ones said: "Be careful of a light commandment as of a heavy one, for you do not know the recompense of the commandments" (m. Avot 2:1). The one conceited with himself is slow in the working of obediences, in self-protection and self-elevation; he does not perceive himself until he falls and tumbles, as He said: "Say to the king and the queen-mother: be lowered, sit down" (Jeremiah 13:18); and He said: "Six are these that the Lord hates… haughty eyes, lying tongue…" (Proverbs 6:16–17).
